entries: Inputs: prescriptions and target constraints, images and anatomical structures, treatment planning systems, beam-modification and immobilization devices, and dose and quality-assurance records.

Verifiable outputs: treatment plans and dose calculations, field and dose-distribution documents, dose verification and quality-assurance records, immobilization and beam-modification device requirements, and dose and implementation records.

Complete workflow: check prescriptions and images → contour and confirm structures → design fields and dose proposals → calculate and verify using applicable methods → quality-assurance records and team review/approval → communicate and oversee implementation. Specific review responsibilities follow organizational procedures.

US radiation therapists deliver irradiation, position patients, and record under physicians' prescriptions and may assist dose procedures and localization. Collaboration overlaps with dosimetrists' planning work; roles are neither absolutely exclusive nor mutually recognized qualifications.

Difference from radiologic technologists: radiologic technologists handle image acquisition and equipment operation; this occupation handles radiotherapy planning and dose verification. Compare planning and implementation responsibilities.

Difference from nuclear medicine technologists: nuclear medicine technologists focus on nuclear imaging and radiopharmaceuticals; this occupation focuses on external-beam and brachytherapy planning and doses.

BLS gives a bachelor’s degree and an accredited dosimetry program as typical U.S. entry preparation. MDCB Route 1 requires at least a bachelor’s degree and graduation from a JRCERT-accredited medical dosimetry program of at least 12 months. Earning the CMD also requires passing the exam. After the September 2025 administration, the international route is limited to the transition for applicants accepted into a program in 2024, with a first attempt no later than January 2027. Check MDCB when applying. January 2027 is the latest first exam administration for that group, not the application deadline. MDCB lists November 2, 2026 as the regular deadline for that exam, with late applications through November 13 limited to U.S. candidates.

Article 7 of China’s radiological diagnosis and treatment rules covers facility staffing. It includes medical physics staff with a bachelor’s degree or higher or an intermediate or higher professional qualification, and lists radiation oncologists and radiation therapists separately. Check hospital postings and job authorization. The U.S. CMD and Chinese facility requirements do not establish equivalence.

Transition path: before changing direction, list transferable skills in plan design, dose verification, quality assurance, and teamwork, alongside physics, standards, and practice knowledge to acquire. Check each against adjacent roles' qualifications and responsibilities.

Honghu People’s Hospital (June 2026) listed one radiation therapy physicist role requiring a full-time bachelor’s degree or higher in biomedical engineering or clinical medicine. Past graduates needed a radiation physicist credential or related certificate. The posting described base pay, performance pay, and allowances without giving an amount.

Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center (July 2026) listed one radiation therapy physicist role at master’s level or above, with plan design, equipment quality control, dose verification, and AI development among the duties and requirements. It did not publish pay. These are historical examples of adjacent roles.

locale_requirements.credential_boundary: Article 7 of China’s radiological diagnosis and treatment rules covers facility staffing. It includes medical physics staff with a bachelor’s degree or higher or an intermediate or higher professional qualification, and lists radiation oncologists and radiation therapists separately. Check hospital postings and job authorization. The U.S. CMD and Chinese facility requirements do not establish equivalence.
locale_requirements.jurisdiction: Check US Programs and CMD Conditions Separately from Chinese Organizational Authorization
locale_requirements.summary: BLS gives a bachelor’s degree and an accredited dosimetry program as typical U.S. entry preparation. MDCB Route 1 requires at least a bachelor’s degree and graduation from a JRCERT-accredited medical dosimetry program of at least 12 months. Earning the CMD also requires passing the exam. After the September 2025 administration, the international route is limited to the transition for applicants accepted into a program in 2024, with a first attempt no later than January 2027. Check MDCB when applying. January 2027 is the latest first exam administration for that group, not the application deadline. MDCB lists November 2, 2026 as the regular deadline for that exam, with late applications through November 13 limited to U.S. candidates.

items.answer: US O*NET Job Zone 4 describes occupational-group preparation, typically a four-year bachelor's degree with exceptions; experience descriptions are not uniform occupational durations. BLS: this occupation typically requires a bachelor's degree and completion of an accredited medical dosimetry program. Employers usually require/prefer CMD, and programs include supervised clinical experience. MDCB's exam eligibility overview requires at least a bachelor's degree in any discipline and graduation from a JRCERT-accredited medical dosimetry program lasting at least 12 months. This page does not claim to have read the full application handbook. Check Chinese appointments, training, and authorization separately; US conditions do not establish Chinese recognition. This page centers on 29-2036.00 plan design, dose calculation/verification, and team communication. O*NET reported titles include Medical Physicist, but names confer no qualified medical physicist status. Official tasks also include supervising or performing localization imaging and radioactivity measurements, so classification cannot establish that all dosimetrists never participate in related operations. AAMD's occupational overview assigns treatment modality/dose decisions and plan review/approval to radiation oncologists, with team quality assurance before implementation. Task overlap does not confer prescribing, independent approval, or cross-role authorization. Check local and organizational scopes.

risks.consequence: May affect treatment safety and effectiveness.
risks.mitigation: If values or transfer records disagree, preserve the originals and refer the discrepancy to the authorized team under facility procedures.
If a boundary is unclear, document the question and refer it to authorized staff for review under facility procedures.

When calibration or quality assurance status is uncertain, refer it to the responsible qualified medical physicist under facility procedures. Dosimetrists perform or assist with checks within their authorization and under direction.
If a check or approval is missing at handoff, document the unresolved item and refer it to authorized staff under facility procedures.
